task.title: Add a Rust-controlled persistent Python execution slice
task.objective: Complete the first vertical slice of issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1021 by keeping Vela's control boundary in Rust while preserving ordinary Python and a live Jupyter kernel as the compute substrate.
acceptance_criteria: Read multiline Python from standard input and preserve it through one explicit adapter, port, and notebook selection.
Parse compact hamelnb JSON and fail without successful partial output on adapter failure, malformed JSON, or non-ok execution status.
Demonstrate retained Python state across two separate Vela CLI invocations against one live notebook.

attempts.summary: Established the Rust process-boundary behavior with a failing test.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused kernel test failed because vela_kernel::python_workbench did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added a process-adapter integration test that requires exact multiline Python, port, and notebook-path forwarding.

attempts.summary: Established the stdin-driven CLI behavior with a failing test.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI test failed because vela-dev rejected the python subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added the python execute command contract before implementing its CLI branch.

attempts.summary: Implemented and verified the first Rust/Python workbench boundary.
attempts.diagnostic: The Rust adapter launches one explicit hamelnb program, validates its compact response, and emits output only after an ok status; the CLI reads Python from stdin.
attempts.patch: Added the focused vela-python-workbench crate, the vela-dev python execute command, fail-closed integration coverage, and boundary documentation.

attempts.summary: Corrected the first staged architecture after independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: Review blocked external-process integration inside vela-kernel and noted Python source exposure through child arguments.
attempts.patch: Moved the boundary into the focused workspace crate required by issue 1021 and changed hamelnb invocation to a permission-restricted temporary code file.

outcome.summary: Vela can now drive ordinary stateful Python through a Rust-controlled command without reimplementing Python or the Jupyter protocol.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-dev --test python_workbench_cli
two nix develop cargo run invocations through localhost scratch.ipynb after crate extraction and code-file forwarding, assigning 80 then evaluating the retained value plus 4

lessons: Rust can own explicit target selection, process failure handling, and response validation while Python remains the compact working language.
Reading source from stdin and forwarding a temporary code file preserves multiline Python without exposing it in child arguments or ordinary argument-size limits.
Persistent notebook state is useful exploratory context but is not verified evidence until replay, provenance, resource bounds, and workspace lifecycle controls exist.
The first slice should integrate the maintained Jupyter adapter rather than reimplementing Python or prematurely owning the full kernel wire protocol.
